title: Parsing JSON in Rust, Go and Python
excerpt: Every language has a favourite way to turn bytes into structured data. Here is the same small task, decoding a user record, written three ways, with the trade-offs each one makes explicit.

content.text: Every language has a favourite way to turn bytes into structured data. Here is the same small task, decoding a user record, written three ways, with the trade-offs each one makes explicit.
Serde derives the decoder at compile time, so mistakes in field names are compile errors rather than runtime surprises.
Go uses struct tags and reflection. It is less strict than Serde, but the standard library is all you need and it compiles in a second.
Python needs no declarations at all; the price is that nothing checks the shape until you touch it, which is why dataclasses and pydantic exist.

blocks.code:
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass

data = json.loads('{"name": "Ann", "age": 41}')
print(data["name"])
